stories.title: Dubai office building receives top smart rating
stories.summary: Dubai’s Al Shera’a, the new headquarters for the Dubai Electricity and Water Authority, is the first building to secure the SPIRE DIAMOND smart rating. The facility uses over 110,000 sensors to manage its systems. The rating is the highest distinction offered by the SPIRE Smart Building programme.

stories.title: WAM
stories.summary: Al Shera’a becomes world’s first building to achieve SPIRE DIAMOND rating for smart buildings www.wam.ae The full piece is for subscribers, and the headline is all that is public for now.

stories.title: Cimpor showcases decarbonisation tech at COP31
stories.summary: Cimpor is participating in COP31 in Antalya to promote low-carbon construction materials and industrial decarbonisation. The company is sharing its expertise in financing and technology alongside OYAK Çimento. The conference brings together world leaders to discuss global sustainability goals and carbon emissions reductions.

stories.title: Porsche Design Tower Bangkok earns LEED precertification
stories.summary: The 22-residence Porsche Design Tower Bangkok has achieved LEED Gold Precertification from the US Green Building Council. Scheduled for completion in December 2028, the project is currently undergoing design-stage reviews. Developers intend to apply for full certification once the tower is finished.

stories.title: Climate finance pledges drop 70 percent
stories.summary: Public funding pledged to assist developing nations with climate change has fallen by over 70 percent in 2026, according to Carbon Brief. Most previous multi-year pledges expired in 2025. Only five nations have announced new commitments, with the UK remaining the only major donor.

stories.title: Passivhaus projects quadruple in Australia
stories.summary: Certified Passivhaus projects in Australia have grown from 48 in 2022 to 201 as of October 2026. The buildings include homes, schools, and commercial facilities. More than 40 sites will host public tours in November to mark International Passivhaus Open Days.

stories.title: Architects coalition urges national retrofit programme
stories.summary: A coalition of 23 built environment organisations, led by the RIBA, has written to energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh. The group is calling for a long-term national retrofit programme as COP31 begins in Turkey. The letter emphasises the need for stronger support for whole-life carbon reduction.

stories.title: EmiratesGBC honors regional sustainability champions at the 14th MENA Green Building Awards
stories.summary: Dubai, UAE: Emirates Green Building Council (EmiratesGBC), a professional non-profit organization dedicated to advancing green building principles in the UAE, celebrated regional excellence and best practices in the built environment at the 14th Annual MENA Green Building Awards 2026. Organized in partnership with MENA Green

stories.title: Geopolymer concrete study reports high strength
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a low-carbon concrete mixture using fly ash and GGBS that reached 68.4 MPa strength after 56 days. The study, published in Scientific Reports, combined CO2 curing with machine learning. The authors note the paper is awaiting final editing and should not be considered conclusive.

stories.title: Hyderabad official defends lake demolition drive
stories.summary: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy has defended the demolition of structures encroaching on Hyderabad lakes. The government claims the drive is necessary to prevent urban flooding and restore water bodies. Officials also plan to develop a lake economy along the Musi river.

stories.title: Cabinet approves development of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at North and South Block Complex, New Delhi
stories.summary: Cabinet approves development of Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at North and South Block Complex, New Delhi New Delhi [India], November 11 (ANI): The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, today has approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat

stories.title: Cabinet approves museum for New Delhi
stories.summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at the North and South Block complex. The project is estimated to cost 3,230 crore. The museum will be housed in the historic buildings to showcase India’s cultural and civilisational heritage.

stories.title: Bhakra Dam museum scheduled for 2027
stories.summary: The Bhakra Beas Management Board is developing a museum in Nangal to preserve the heritage of the Bhakra Dam. The project is expected to cost 9 crore and aims to increase tourism in the township. Construction on the site has already commenced.

stories.title: Why Do Jaipur’s Streets Run in Straight Lines? A King & a Scholar Planned It 300 Years Ago
stories.summary: Google Maps went live on 8 February, 2005, but a Rajput king had planned an entire city around a grid 278 years earlier. When Sawai Jai Singh II founded Jaipur in 1727, he laid out straight streets that crossed at right angles, divided the city

stories.title: Odisha signs planning agreement for transport vision
stories.summary: The government of Odisha has signed a memorandum of understanding with the School of Planning and Architecture in Bhopal. The partnership aims to create a vision document for transport infrastructure across water, rail, and air sectors to support the Viksit Odisha 2036 initiative.

stories.title: Lavasa hill city denied environmental clearance
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Environment and Forests has denied environmental clearance to the Lavasa project. The ministry stated that clearance cannot be granted until the Maharashtra government takes action regarding previous environmental law violations. Construction at the site was halted last year.

stories.title: Archohm: Indian Contemporary Architecture
stories.summary: This publication compiles 25 years of work by Studio Archohm, highlighting their evolution into key players in Indian nation-building through large-scale urban, infrastructure, and civic projects, alongside private-sector experimentation. The studio's multidisciplinary portfolio spans design research, city branding, education, and experience design, connecting scales from

stories.title: Hafeez Contractor to design NSE headquarters
stories.summary: Architect Hafeez Contractor has been selected to design the National Stock Exchange’s new headquarters in Mumbai’s Bandra Kurla Complex. The project will cover approximately 10,995 square metres. The exchange describes the building as a symbol of India’s growing presence in global financial markets.

stories.title: Devon Passivhaus uses reclaimed materials
stories.summary: McLean Quinlan designed the 388 square metre Devon Passivhaus using reclaimed terracotta, rough-sawn oak, and clay plaster. The project, certified by Etude, features triple-glazed timber windows and a dark render. It is located in Exeter, United Kingdom, and was completed in 2018.

stories.title: Javier De Las Heras Solé completes Súria Library
stories.summary: The Súria Library in Catalonia, Spain, was completed in 2026. Designed by Javier de las Heras Solé for the Súria City Council, the project involved a team of architects and technical specialists. The building serves as a new cultural facility for the local municipality.

stories.title: Counterspace to design Elie Khouri Art Foundation
stories.summary: Architect Sumayya Vally and her practice Counterspace will transform a Jumeirah villa into the permanent home for the Elie Khouri Art Foundation. The Dubai project, which includes galleries and gardens, is scheduled to open in late 2028. The design draws on traditional Gulf courtyard houses.

stories.title: Shenzhen Opera House construction continues
stories.summary: Ateliers Jean Nouvel is developing the Shenzhen Opera House, a 220,000 square metre cultural complex in China. Titled Light of the Sea, the project features a roof inspired by the movement of the sea. Completion is expected by December 2028.

stories.title: Chartier-Corbasson transforms Paris tunnel into restrooms
stories.summary: French studio Chartier-Corbasson Architectes has converted an underground passage beneath the Trocadero Gardens into public toilets. The project uses stainless and weathered steel to elevate the ordinary. It is part of the OnE masterplan to develop public spaces surrounding the Eiffel Tower.

stories.title: Snøhetta reveals masterplan for Istanbul coast
stories.summary: The 84-hectare Ion Riva masterplan in Beykoz brings together Snøhetta, Bjarke Ingels Group, and MVRDV to build a community for 3,000 people. Snøhetta’s contribution includes a circular building called The Ring. The project prioritizes natural topography to maximize views toward the Black Sea.

stories.title: Sumayya Vally to lead Dubai villa transformation
stories.summary: The Elie Khouri Art Foundation has appointed Sumayya Vally of Counterspace to design its permanent home in Dubai. The project will repurpose a villa in the Jumeirah 1 district into a contemporary art institution. It is scheduled to open in late 2028.

stories.title: PPAA completes twin houses in Mexico
stories.summary: Pérez Palacios Arquitectos Asociados has completed two 500 square metre houses in Valle de Bravo, Mexico. The project, called Rejas, uses concrete and glued-laminated timber. Founder Pablo Pérez Palacios described the design as an argument for building less in a landscape he says is overbuilt.

stories.title: Icelandic viewpoint draws on Viking legend
stories.summary: Arkibygg Architects and Esja Architecture designed the Ring of Bjólfur, a mountain viewpoint in Seyðisfjörður, Iceland. The structure is shaped like a silver ring to evoke the burial site of a legendary Viking settler. It provides access to a ridge on Mount Bjólfur.

stories.title: Prusa releases ESD-safe 3D printing filament
stories.summary: Prusa has launched a PETG filament filled with carbon fiber and carbon nanotubes designed to dissipate electrostatic energy. While targeted at electronics manufacturing, the company notes the material is cheaper than its non-ESD carbon fiber alternative. It is intended for protecting static-sensitive electronics.

stories.title: Ecocem invests in Benelux expansion
stories.summary: Ecocem is marking 25 years in the Benelux region with a 12 million euro investment in Moerdijk. The company is also introducing three new low-carbon cement solutions. The firm continues to focus on its established strategy for low-carbon construction materials.

stories.title: Mass timber adoption grows among developers
stories.summary: Developers are increasingly looking toward mass timber as an alternative to traditional steel and concrete construction. The material is gaining ground in the industry as a viable option for large-scale building projects.

stories.title: Timber industry pushes for mass timber data centres
stories.summary: Southern growers are advocating for mass timber in data centres and hotels to address a timber glut caused by sluggish home building. With four mill closures in Georgia leaving millions of tons of wood without a buyer, the industry is seeking new demand for its supply.

stories.title: India and Norway collaborate on waste-to-resource projects
stories.summary: India and Norway are exploring joint research to convert industrial and construction waste into building materials. The initiative, organized by CSIR and SINTEF, aims to promote sustainable construction. Representatives met in New Delhi to discuss waste management solutions for the cement and construction sectors.

stories.title: Glulam market projected to reach 13.5 billion dollars
stories.summary: The global glue laminated timber market is expected to grow from 7.9 billion dollars in 2025 to 13.5 billion dollars by 2035. Analysts cite green building certifications and sustainable material adoption as primary drivers. China is currently leading growth at a 7.5 percent rate.

stories.title: U.S. mass timber projects see significant increase
stories.summary: The number of mass timber buildings in the U.S. has risen more than 15-fold over the last decade, surpassing 1,500 projects. WoodWorks reports that developers are using the material for offices, libraries, and apartments. Mass timber panels are used for floor, ceiling, and load-bearing structures.

stories.title: Wave-shaped surfaces reduce wind pressure in tests
stories.summary: Researchers at the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering found that wave-shaped roof and wall geometries can reduce peak wind pressure by up to 60 percent. The study suggests that altering building design could improve storm protection. The team tested the shapes inside a wind tunnel.

stories.title: Aectual partners with Caracol for 3D printing
stories.summary: Dutch studio Aectual is using Caracol’s Heron AM robotic platforms to 3D print circular architectural products globally. By utilizing a distributed manufacturing network, the company aims to keep production close to its clients. The first parts are currently in production.

stories.title: Northeast urban planning faces geographical hurdles
stories.summary: Deputy Chief Minister Chowna Mein stated that urban planning in the Northeast must account for unique geographical and administrative realities. He argued that conventional parameters like population and area fail to reflect the actual cost of delivering municipal services in difficult, mountainous terrain with scattered settlements.

stories.title: Winter fog patterns differ across Indian cities
stories.summary: Delhi, Lucknow and Patna frequently experience dense winter fog, while Bengaluru and Hyderabad remain largely clear. The difference is attributed to more than just temperature, with geography, wind speed and moisture levels playing significant roles in determining why some cities wake up under a persistent blanket.

stories.title: India faces complex water security challenge
stories.summary: India’s water challenge is no longer limited to household tap access. Experts suggest the country must secure adequate, affordable water without depleting natural systems. Water serves as a basic necessity, industrial resource and foundation for public health, meaning shortages carry costs that extend beyond the water sector.

stories.title: Energy conservation code remains unnotified in Jammu
stories.summary: Despite a February 2025 announcement by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah to prioritise energy efficiency, the Energy Conservation Building Code remains unnotified. The file is currently with the Power Development Department, even after consultations with the Department of Law and the Public Works Department were completed.

stories.title: Monsoon Onset Gets a New Climate-Network Method
stories.summary: The arrival of the monsoon is often treated as a date on a calendar: the first rains appear, the season is declared, and public agencies begin acting on that signal. A new study by the Indian Institute of Technology Madras and Gauhati University argues that

stories.title: Lucknow approves 431 crore development package
stories.summary: The Lucknow Development Authority approved a 431 crore package for four multi-level parking facilities, a Metro yard and hospital expansion. The facilities are expected to accommodate over 1,500 vehicles. The approvals were granted during the authority's 188th board meeting held on November 2.

stories.title: Kashmir musk deer habitat faces climate threat
stories.summary: A new study projects that climate change could reduce suitable habitat for the endangered Kashmir musk deer by 82.6 percent by 2100 under high-emissions scenarios. Potential wildlife corridors may contract by half, increasing the risk of population isolation as most climate refugia lie outside protected areas.

stories.title: Consumer panel orders Bombay Realty refund
stories.summary: The Maharashtra Consumer Commission ordered Bombay Dyeing and Bombay Realty to refund 1.95 crore to two homebuyers. The commission observed that developers cannot retain public funds while failing to meet delivery deadlines. The ruling follows complaints regarding delays and unreasonable financial requests from the developer.

stories.title: Smart rain barrels tested for urban runoff
stories.summary: A simulation-based study in the journal City and Built Environment evaluated smart rain barrels to manage stormwater in high-density areas. Researchers used the PySWMM model to determine if integrating smart technology could overcome the storage limitations of traditional fixed-capacity systems during continuous rainfall events.

stories.title: Ocean Shores declares emergency after storm damage
stories.summary: The mayor of Ocean Shores issued an emergency declaration as powerful storms caused significant erosion and threatened coastal property. Residents reported that high tides and wind-driven waves pushed further inland than expected. Officials have urged the public to stay off beaches while the storm persists.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh expands smart city initiatives
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is managing technology-driven urban development across 17 cities. Ten cities were selected under the Centre’s Smart Cities Mission, while seven others were added via a state-level scheme in 2019. The initiatives focus on traffic management, sanitation and the delivery of citizen-centric services.

stories.title: Beyond Smart Homes: How Smart City Projects Are Reshaping Urban Real Estate
stories.summary: A township can serve a family from the time children start school to the years when their parents grow older. From smart mobility and digital infrastructure to sustainable energy management, healthcare, education and green spaces, smart city developments are seeking to address the evolving needs

stories.title: Raipur plans deployment of 240 electric buses
stories.summary: Raipur is set to deploy 240 electric buses across four cities. The capital's real estate sector has grown significantly, with annual trade rising to approximately 5,000 crore. Buyer demand for luxury housing has surged by 70 percent, with residents increasingly seeking premium flats in high-rise towers.

stories.title: Machine learning maps urban heat disparities
stories.summary: A study in Computational Urban Science suggests that integrating neighborhood context and architectural geometry into machine learning algorithms improves the mapping of urban microclimates. Researchers evaluated methodologies across Indianapolis and Bloomington by contrasting satellite imagery against models that incorporate three-dimensional urban form parameters.

stories.title: Karnataka govt plans to develop Bengaluru as an international Smart City: CM Bommai
stories.summary: The Karnataka government has long term plans of developing Bengaluru as an international Smart City by developing Metro, Suburban Rail, good roads and satellite towns using advanced technology, Chief Minister Basavaraj Bommai said.The CM in his address after laying the foundation stone for 'Masti Bhavan'

stories.summary: The entire country is proud of what Jammu and Kashmir has achieved in the last four years, Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha said here on Saturday. At an event organised as part of the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra in Srinagar on January 6, he expressed gratitude

stories.summary: Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue When Federal Emergency Management Agency models failed to capture chronic neighborhood flooding, Savannah sought data from affected communities to solve longstanding drainage problems. stories.title: Israel startups target 76 percent landfill rate
stories.summary: A report from PLANETech details 80 startups attempting to address Israel's waste management crisis. According to a July 2025 report by the State Comptroller, 76 percent of municipal waste still goes to landfill. Municipalities are now looking to the tech sector to transform traditional waste management models.

stories.title: Trimble updates construction software and drone platform
stories.summary: Trimble announced new capabilities for its Connect platform, including scheduling AI and document review tools. The company also debuted its WorksManager drone processing software, which allows civil contractors to process drone data in the cloud. The updates were revealed at the company's annual Dimensions conference in Las Vegas.

stories.title: Homebuilders use 3D printing to rebuild in Altadena
stories.summary: A builder is using a gantry crane to 3D print concrete walls for homes destroyed by the 2025 Eaton Fire. The project, led by Emergent Home, uses technology from the Dutch firm COBOD to extrude concrete layers. The builder was originally founded to assist with post-fire reconstruction efforts.

stories.summary: Turning a Simple Idea Into a 3D Printed Object: How AI Is Changing the Creative Process From the first rough concept to a physical prototype, explore how AI-powered 3D generation can make digital design more accessible while introducing new challenges for creators. stories.title: Archiboost secures $6.2 million for AI document review
stories.summary: Archiboost raised $6.2 million in funding led by Hanabi Capital and Marathon Venture Capital. The company plans to use the capital to develop a connected model of building information that links design elements to governing requirements. The platform aims to help AEC teams identify errors in construction documents.

stories.title: Building an AI-ready construction industry: The devil is in the data
stories.summary: René Wolf, CEO of RIB Software, explores why construction firms risk wasting AI investment and eroding profitability if they fail to address fragmented data, disconnected workflows and inconsistent processes Artificial intelligence is rapidly climbing the construction industry’s agenda. From predicting project delays to automating reporting,

stories.title: Creality releases AI-enabled 3D printer for children
stories.summary: Creality has launched the mBox, a $329 compact 3D printer marketed to children aged six to 16. The system features kid-safe components and is being sold exclusively through TikTok Shop in the United States until December 10. It is positioned as a holiday gift for young users.

stories.title: Ageiro launches Ark Watcher for project monitoring
stories.summary: Ageiro has introduced Ark Watcher, a tool within its project intelligence platform that monitors data across systems like Procore, SharePoint, and Autodesk Forma. The software tracks project conditions and potential risks to reduce the need for manual checks. It aims to identify issues that require human review.

stories.title: Amy Catania Kulper named dean at UVA School of Architecture
stories.summary: Amy Catania Kulper will become the dean of the University of Virginia School of Architecture on January 6. Kulper, a historian and curator who currently leads the Bartlett School of Architecture, succeeds Malo Hutson. She will also hold the Elson Professorship pending board approval.

stories.title: David Brian Hill appointed dean at UH architecture college
stories.summary: David Brian Hill has been named the next dean of the University of Houston's Gerald D. Hines College of Architecture and Design, effective February 1, 2027. Hill, a veteran educator and researcher, will succeed Patricia Belton Oliver, who is retiring from the position later that year.

stories.summary: Amy Catania Kulper, a historian-theorist, designer, curator and academic leader who most recently led the Bartlett School of Architecture at University College London, has been named the next dean of the University of Virginia’s School of Architecture, effective Jan. 6. stories.title: Student develops 3D-printed bricks from lunar regolith
stories.summary: A University of Arkansas student has developed a method for 3D printing bricks using lunar regolith. The project aims to address the high cost of transporting building materials to the moon by utilizing local lunar dust, potentially enabling the construction of structures resilient to cosmic radiation and moonquakes.

research.title: Data-driven regional traffic simulation from heterogeneous mobility sources
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Regional traffic simulators increasingly combine mobile-phone, road-sensor and GPS data, but what each source contributes is rarely clear. We present an agent-based simulator of daily traffic in Emilia-Romagna, Italy: phone data give trips and their timing. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Everything in its right place: attention is a radio head
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Attention, the core of language models, is a digital calculation over tokens: an exponential selects them, a division normalizes and a positional code sets the order. We show that attention can instead emerge from the synchronization. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Evolution of cooperation in enterprise resource-sharing networks with dynamic participation and adaptive decision-making
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Resource sharing among enterprises is an important mechanism for improving resource utilization efficiency and facilitating collaborative development. However, the emergence and sustainability of cooperative behavior depend critically on whether enterprises choose to participate in resource-sharing activities. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: NASA reveals Earth's ozone hole has grown to a size not seen in a decade
research.summary: The Antarctic ozone hole expanded to its seventh-largest size on record in 2026, driven by unusual weather conditions that pushed it close to its historic maximum. Scientists say international restrictions on ozone-destroying chemicals prevented even greater damage, and Earth's protective ozone layer is still recovering.

research.title: Oscillations in two-stage contagion on networks: contagion structure, turnover and connectivity
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two-stage contagion describes processes, such as the adoption of an opinion or of a technological novelty, in which an individual must be exposed to an adopter twice before adopting. With demographic turnover these processes can generate. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Phase transitions in the simplicial Ising model on hypergraphs
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Complex higher-order interactions can reshape higher-order dynamics in complex systems. Systematic understanding of the repertoire of phase transitions that higher-order interactions can trigger remains incomplete. Here we study the phase transitions in the simplicial Ising model. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Spatial Selection and the Multiscale Dynamics of Urban Change
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Growth is a multi-layered phenomenon in human societies, composed of socioeconomic and demographic change at many different scales. Yet, standard macroeconomic indicators average over most of these processes, blurring the spatial and hierarchical heterogeneity driving people's. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
